findings: ST elevation with Q waves in the anterior leads
Reciprocal ST depression in inferior leads

echoTasks.find: Anterior septal and anterior wall akinesis with compensatory hyperkinesis of remote segments
Apical akinesis with reduced ejection fraction in proportion to the involved segments
Apical and anterior wall akinesis confirmed in the two chamber window

exam.other: Lungs clear, no added sounds, blood sugar 210 mg per dl on glucometer
exam.precordium: Localised apex beat, dyskinetic impulse at the left sternal edge
exam.pulse: Regular 96, normal volume, equal on both sides

keyPoints: Activate reperfusion immediately per the ACC and AHA STEMI guideline, with primary PCI preferred where transfer is rapid
Give aspirin 300 mg chewed at once then 75 mg daily, plus high intensity atorvastatin 80 mg daily, per the same guideline
Start anticoagulation only if a thrombus protocol applies, and screen for mechanical complications daily
Optimise glycaemic control and counsel on beedi cessation with a quit date
Plan predischarge echo, rehab enrolment, and dual antiplatelet education with bleed advice
management.model: Emergency reperfusion with guideline antiplatelet and statin therapy, complication watch, and secondary prevention

stem: A 56 year old interstate bus driver reaches a district hospital 6 hours after crushing retrosternal pain with sweating. The ECG shows ST elevation with reciprocal depression.
teaching: Territory rules the read: anterior akinesis with anterior ST elevation localises the left anterior descending artery
Moderate means 4 to 6 abnormal segments, and function falls in proportion to the count
Compensatory hyperkinesis of remote segments is expected early and must not inflate the EF read
Reperfusion plus aspirin 300 mg then 75 mg daily plus atorvastatin 80 mg daily is the resident level backbone
title: Anterior myocardial infarction with moderate wall motion abnormality
